review.headline: A wild sacrificial attack nearly worked before the clock ran out

sections.text: You chose an aggressive path early in the Italian Game with the speculative sacrifice 8.Bxf7+? Kxf7 9.Ng5+??, hoping to blow open Black's king. After 10.Qf3+?, Black slipped with 10...Nf6??, allowing you to strike back instantly.

You punished their slip with 11.e5!, revealing a discovered attack against c6 from your queen on f3. When Black blundered again with 11...Nxd4??, you capitalized immediately by taking the loose rook with 12.Qxa8! to establish a pin on c8 and take a commanding lead.

Holding the advantage required patience, but with the clock ticking down, you traded down with 17.Qxf6+?? Qxf6 18.Rxf6+ Kg7. That liquidated your attack and left you down a pawn, ultimately losing on time.

review.turning_point: After winning a full rook, you gave away your entire advantage with 17.Qxf6+??, letting Black simplify into an active endgame where you ran out of time.
review.focus: Avoid premature piece sacrifices like 8.Bxf7+? unless you have calculated a concrete, forced continuation.
